<reason>CON won by breaking PRO's false choice between blanket by-right and a housing ban. CON showed conditional planning can add abundant housing on parking lots, commercial strips, and wealthy lots without creating a speculative demolition premium over occupied low-rent buildings. PRO's replacement and relocation mandates were then exposed as internally strained: interim homes must be found amid the claimed shortage, costly mandates invite pre-permit buyouts and evictions, and PRO's claim that unprofitable teardowns simply will not occur concedes much of CON's targeted alternative. PRO effectively answered status-quo displacement, but never closed those evasion and feasibility gaps.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: it answered that conditional denial removes the speculative premium, then turned PRO's interim-housing and “option, not an order” defenses into evidence for directly targeting density away from vulnerable rentals.</best_rebuttal>
